result:
My verdict for DG0 round 23 is **PASS**, with one new Low, non-mandatory finding (F-DG0-249). This is the QA review of frozen candidate `sha256:e6df2e1e…51c5` (source 6438e20).

**Candidate:** The assignment hash, the candidate ID and a complete (non-shallow) clone all matched. HEAD was the freeze-metadata commit 78954a6. During my run it moved to a6cf38e, which only adds the domain reviewer's run evidence; the candidate ID was unchanged afterwards. I did not open any other round-23 record.

**What I ran:**
- **Existing suites:** all pass.
  - Source extraction check passes.
  - Gate validator tests: 62/62, including the four D-039 tests.
  - Agent tests: 39/39, plus 22 Python tests.
  - `--register DG0`, `--pipeline` and `--reconcile` all pass.
  - The pre-freeze passes 11/11 in a fresh `--no-local` clone.
- **Real-repo dry-run on the full history:** 0 errors in the PRUNED, RECORD-LESS and DROPPED buckets. The output is identical on the `--no-local` clone and the plain local clone. The remaining 59 errors all come from round 23 not being finished yet: pending verifications, the auditor's acceptances, missing round-23 records, and a placeholder field in the draft gate record the script builds.
- **D-039 negative suite:** 11/11, in a new file (`dg0-gate-negative-r23.test.mjs`) with 10 cases that aren't in `tools/gates/tests`:
  - The round-22 exploit (a forged round naming a non-existent commit, closing a High finding with an all-zero `fix_revision`) is now rejected.
  - Missing, null, `unknown` or absent run heads are rejected, in gate and non-gate rounds.
  - A later-round sidecar can't change severity, `mandatory_violation`, requirement or title, and rounds are ordered numerically. An identical re-raise gives no false error.
  - Shallow clones (`--depth=3`, `--shallow-exclude`) are refused; a complete clone is accepted.
  - The one remaining absence tolerance (for round 18's manifest) only applies when the manifest's contents still hash to its candidate ID.
  - My first run of this suite failed one case because of a bug in my own test (a `git clone` argument git doesn't accept). I fixed the test, and the logs say so.
- **Round-22 QA suite re-run unchanged:** 7 pass, 2 fail, both as D-039 intends. The case that asserted the old tolerance now fails, and one case matches on an error message D-039 removed although the logged error is still a rejection. There are no regressions; the analysis is saved.
- **Register:** 412 rows and 0 integrity errors. The 19 DG0-final rows are IMPLEMENTED with existing evidence, and A01–A28 are all covered.
- **Fix commits:** all 110 `fix_revision` values are full 40-hex, present and ancestors of HEAD. The pruned commits `450c756` and `cb76260` are absent in the original repo and in both clones.
- **Agents:** the recorded evidence shows 10 agents loaded, 10 distinct sessions, all on the orchestrator's model. The live guard blocked my Write-tool attempt on `docs/source/QA-PROBE.txt`, and five shell writes to protected paths all failed as read-only.
- **Feasibility:** every A01–A28 has a test level, a first stage and a gate.

**My round-22 findings (all CLOSED_VERIFIED):**

| Finding | Severity | How verified |
|---|---|---|
| F-DG0-246 | Medium | Reproduced, now rejected; new cases and unit tests pass |
| F-DG0-247 | Low | Pruned commits gone in every clone mode; dry-run outputs identical |
| F-DG0-248 | Low | Unit test exists and passes; I added further shallow shapes |

**New finding:**

| ID | Severity | Mandatory violation | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-DG0-249 | Low | No | When a round's commit is recorded as missing, the validator skips the check that the fix is in that round's candidate. So a real fix inside the gate candidate, but not in the history the verifying run started from, can still close a finding. |

For F-DG0-249, the proposal is to also require the fix to be an ancestor of the verifying run's starting commit, which D-039 now requires to be present. No real closure is affected: all 104 closures already meet that rule. The owner is `delivery-orchestrator`.

**Output files** (the runner copies the review files back after the run):
- Review record and sidecars: `docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-23/qa-verifier.json`, `qa-verifier.findings.json`, `qa-verifier.verifications.json`
- Evidence: `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/round-23/`
- New tests: `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/qa/tests/dg0-gate-negative-r23.test.mjs`

The record and both sidecars validate against their schemas, and all 75 evidence paths exist. I deleted all disposable clones.
